name: steel
note: Shipbuilding (mild) steel, the plating's default name: Okun's backing ladder 0.7 (MS).

name: mild steel
note: Mild steel: hull plate, and the splinter decks of the 1890s on. Okun's ladder 0.7 (MS).

name: high-tensile steel
note: HT and Krupp low-nickel structural steel, the laminated decks of 1900-1925: Okun's ladder 0.8 (HT).

name: wrought iron
note: The ironclads' plate and hulls (s.g. 7.6-7.9). Spezia 1876 ~0.50, Tresidder/Thompson 0.56, Okun 0.6 (WI).

name: wood
note: Planking and wooden hulls (oak and teak 0.65-0.75). Okun counts teak at 1/100 of its thickness.

name: aluminium alloy
note: Light alloy deckhouses. [EST] about steel's protection per weight (2.7/7.85); no research row.

name: compound
note: Steel face welded to a wrought-iron back, a third and two thirds (1877-1891). Annapolis < 0.75-0.80; shatters chilled shot only (CMP).

name: nickel steel
note: Homogeneous nickel steel (1889-1896). Annapolis > 0.77-0.83, Johnson's limit 0.92 (NIS).

name: Harvey nickel steel
note: Harveyized: carburized nickel steel, a thin hard face (1891-1899). NO 1937's limit 0.79 (HRV).

name: Krupp cemented
note: KC a/A and its licensees (1894-1918): decremental face-hardened Ni-Cr. Capped trials 0.87-0.97, Okun 0.83 of WWII FH (KCA).

name: Krupp cemented (KC n/A)
note: KC neuer Art, the German plate of 1928-1945. NPG 1946-47 graded it 83-113% (KCNA).

name: cemented armour
note: British (and licensees') KC of 1900-1932: "inferior to KC a/A" (Okun) (BKC).

name: cemented armour (CA)
note: British Cemented Armour of 1933-1945: a thin face on a tough back, slightly better against bigger shells (CA).

name: Vickers cemented
note: VC, Vickers' KC (Japan's of the Kongo and Nagato era): as British WWI KC (BKC).

name: Terni cemented
note: Italian KC before 1918, as British WWI KC (BKC).

name: Terni cemented (1930s)
note: Italian Terni cemented of 1929-1943: the best of the five at 15-18" in Okun's FACEHARD tables; little test data (TKC).

name: Witkowitz cemented
note: Witkowitz KC (Austria-Hungary, 1905-1918): "~95% of WWII FH" (Okun) (WKC).

name: French cemented (1930s)
note: French face-hardened plate of 1932-1945: Okun assumed it equal to US; German tests found it inferior [UNCERTAIN] (FRFH).

name: Class A armour
note: US face-hardened plate before the thick chill (Pennsylvania, Colorado: KC-type). [EST] as KC a/A; no research row.

name: Class A
note: US Class A of 1933-1945, the thick chill: FACEHARD (NL) 1.03 at 8", 0.92 at 16"; OS 751 agrees (USA).

name: Vickers hardened
note: Japanese VH of 1937-1945, only over 11": FACEHARD NL 0.89-0.90; Shinano's 26" plate ~0.8 (VH).

name: Krupp non-cemented
note: KNC, Krupp-type homogeneous Ni-Cr (1894-1925): Okun 0.95 homogeneous to WWI (KNC).

name: special treatment steel
note: US Class B and STS of 1910-1932 (CB1).

name: Class B
note: US Class B of the 1930s and WWII: the standard (STS).

name: STS
note: US special treatment steel of 1930-1945, the scale's reference: NPG Class B 91-106% (STS).

name: non-cemented armour
note: British NCA of 1926-1945 (NCA).

name: Wotan hart
note: Wotan hart (1925-1945), 18% elongation: 0.85 against a 16" (WH).

name: Wotan
note: Wotan weich (1925-1945), the softer deck plate (WW).

name: Molybdenum steel
note: Japanese homogeneous NVNC/CNC (1926-1945): Okun's M79 Q 0.97.

name: special steel
note: French homogeneous deck plate of the 1930s. [EST] as Japanese NVNC; no research row.
